content: 1. Family Planning and Nutritional Support: Women should be referred for family planning counseling. A three-month supply of iron should be dispensed, and the patient should be counseled on the importance of compliance with the treatment. If tetanus immunization is incomplete, it should be administered. The use of impregnated bed nets for both the mother and baby should be promoted to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. All actions and findings should be recorded in the mother’s home-based maternal record. 2. Postpartum Care and Hypertension Management: For severe hypertension, administer appropriate antihypertensive medication and refer the patient urgently to a hospital. For moderate hypertension, reassess in one week. If it persists, refer the patient to a hospital. 3. Anemia Assessment and Management: Look for conjunctival and palmar pallor. For severe anemia, provide a double dose of iron (60 mg twice daily for three months), refer urgently to a hospital, and follow up in two weeks to monitor progress and compliance. For moderate anemia, provide a double dose of iron for three months and reassess at the next postnatal visit (in four weeks). If anemia persists, refer to a hospital. If no anemia is present, continue iron supplementation for a total of three months. 4. HIV Testing and Counseling: If the woman has not been tested for HIV or does not know her status, offer routine HIV testing and counseling. Explain the benefits of knowing her status, the confidentiality of results, and the routine nature of the test. If the woman is HIV-positive, provide counseling on the implications of the diagnosis, refer her to HIV services for further assessment and treatment, and counsel on infant feeding options, family planning, safer sex practices, and partner testing. Provide emotional support and follow up in two weeks. If the woman is HIV-negative, counsel her on staying negative through safer sex practices and partner testing. If the woman refuses testing or does not disclose her status, counsel her on safer sex practices and partner testing. 5. Management of Postpartum Bleeding and Infections: For heavy or light vaginal bleeding after six weeks, refer the patient to a hospital. For fever or foul-smelling lochia, assess for uterine infection by checking for abdominal tenderness, abnormal lochia, and elevated temperature. If uterine infection is suspected, administer IV fluids and antibiotics and refer urgently to a hospital. For upper urinary tract infections, administer appropriate IV/IM antibiotics and refer urgently to a hospital. For lower urinary tract infections, provide oral antibiotics, encourage increased fluid intake, and follow up in two days. If no improvement, refer to a hospital. 6. Management of Febrile Illnesses: For very severe febrile disease, insert an IV line, administer appropriate IV/IM antibiotics, and provide antimalarial treatment (artemether or quinine) and glucose. Refer urgently to a hospital. For malaria, provide oral antimalarial medication and follow up in two days. If no improvement, refer to a hospital. 7. Management of Vaginal Discharge: Assess for itching, abnormal discharge, and partner symptoms. If gonorrhea or chlamydia infection is suspected, treat both the woman and her partner with appropriate antibiotics and counsel on safer sex practices. For suspected candida infection, provide clotrimazole and counsel on safer sex practices. If no improvement, refer to a hospital. For bacterial or trichomonas infection, provide metronidazole and counsel on safer sex practices. 8. Breast Problems: Refer to specific guidelines for managing breast issues. 9. Respiratory Symptoms: For cough or breathing difficulty, assess the duration, presence of chest pain, blood in sputum, and signs of breathlessness or wheezing. If pneumonia is suspected, administer the first dose of IV/IM antibiotics and refer urgently to a hospital. For chronic lung disease, refer to a hospital for assessment. Counsel on smoking cessation and avoiding second-hand smoke. 10. Tuberculosis Management: If her sputum is TB-positive within two months of delivery, plan to provide INH prophylaxis to the newborn. Offer HIV testing if not already done and counsel on smoking cessation and avoiding second-hand smoke. Screen close contacts for tuberculosis. 11. Postpartum Depression and Emotional Well-being: Counsel her partner and family to assist her. Follow up in two weeks and refer if no improvement. For postpartum depression (usually after two weeks), provide emotional support and refer urgently to a hospital. 12. General Postpartum Examination: Assess the mother’s overall well-being, including any pain, fever, bleeding, or urinary problems. Check for complications during delivery, current treatments, and HIV status. If all findings are normal, provide counseling on postpartum care, hygiene, nutrition, and family planning. Reinforce safer sex practices and advise on when to seek care. 13. Documentation and Follow-up: Record all findings, treatments, and advice in the mother’s home-based record.
